Study exercise derived from this source. Explain the approach in your own words, work through an example, and identify edge cases. For code, implement your own version and discuss its time and space complexity.

#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

class Solution {
public:
    string convert(string s, int numRows) {
        string res;
        // base case
        if (s.empty() || numRows <= 1)
            return s;

        // handle first row
        for (int i = 0; i < s.size(); i += (numRows - 1) * 2)
            res.push_back(s[i]);

        // handle middle rows
        for (int j = 1; j < numRows - 1; j++)
        {
            bool down = true;
            for (int i = j; i < s.size();)  // Since the step has two possible values, so not add increase logic here.
            {
                res.push_back(s[i]); // Add first element of current row, then add others
                if (down) // going down
                    i += (numRows - 1 - j) * 2;
                else // going up
                    i += 2*j;

                down = !down; // switch direction
            }
        }

        // handle last row
        for (int i = numRows - 1; i < s.size(); i += (numRows - 1) * 2)
            res.push_back(s[i]);

        return res;
    }
};

// Test
int main()
{
    Solution sol;
    string s = "PAYPALISHIRING";
    int numRows = 4;
    auto res = sol.convert(s, numRows);
    cout << res << endl;
    
    return 0;
}
